summary: Five retractions plus a source audit of Theorem AC; no compute, no Lean. RETRACTIONS: BinaryCenter means the palette HITS the fixed pair, not contains it; the four-state field DOES hit {0,5} a.e., so my inapplicability claim was false; B2 means each palette card<=2, not all palettes in one 2-set; Bool coarsenings of 4 states number 16, so my 'no Bool coarsening satisfies RealState' proposition is FALSE - s=[f in {0,1}] gives RealState with J={0}, K={5} and does flip, and hcard is what fails (univ\({0}u{5}) has 4 > 2 elements); and a model omitting a hypothesis does not refute the theorem assuming it, so 'the field refutes (MS)' and all broad no-go sentences are withdrawn.  AUDIT: all eight of AC's citations resolve (ApproachingContinuum AngularBoundary:235 with a common v; Straddle :147; spatialSupport :308; outer/inner_strip :244,:252; continuum_outer/inner_restriction :259,:279 concluding a HIT; binary_strip_palette_rigidity BoundaryTrace:280 with independent side bools; angleBoundary_nonempty :381, angleBoundary_six :435, sixAngle_injective :423). Steps (a)-(d) are supported, one flagged place: collapsing the per-index H i into a single J. The field lacks all four strip data AC needs and fails exactly at t=0, where its {0,5} choice jumps 5 to 0 - the essential local constancy rigidity forces. Consumer: q=(0,3,3,3,0,0) has v1=v2=v3=-1, one common direction, leaving {0,5}. AC is not F6.

verified_results.statement: RETRACTION R1: BinaryCenter c hc x i j := for a.e. t, t in paletteSet x i OR t in paletteSet x j (BinaryPalettes.lean:9), i.e. the palette HITS the pair. My 'palette contained in the pair' reading is withdrawn.

RETRACTION R2: the four-state field satisfies BinaryCenter x 0 5 a.e., since {0,2} and {0,3} contain 0 and {3,5} and {2,5} contain 5. So my claim that no BinaryCenter pair exists and binary_centers_separated is inapplicable is FALSE and withdrawn.

RETRACTION R3: B2 means each palette has cardinality <= 2 (satisfied by the field at every direction), not that all palettes lie in a single 2-set. Conflation withdrawn; the 'no 2-set contains all four palettes' test tested the wrong property.

RETRACTION R4: the previous block's proposition 'no Bool coarsening of the field satisfies both RealState premises' is FALSE. There are 16 Bool maps on four states; s = [f in {0,1}] gives RealState with J={0} (intersection of palettes {0,2},{0,3}) and K={5} (intersection of {3,5},{2,5}), and it does flip at 60 degrees since f -> f+2 maps {0,1} to {2,3}. The premise that fails is hcard: univ \({0}u{5}) = {1,2,3,4} has cardinality 4 > 2. In general distinct palettes here share at most one label, so every RealState level set admits at most one label and |J u K| <= 2. The binding premise is hcard, not RealState.
verified_results.grade: self-retraction; the corrected analysis is PROOF by inspection of the four palettes

verified_results.statement: RETRACTION R5: 'the multi-state candidate (MS) is REFUTED by Astra's field' is withdrawn, since the field omits the state-determination hypothesis and therefore is not a counterexample to (MS). All broad no-go sentences of the previous block are frozen and withdrawn as statements ('no purely state-theoretic generalisation can close the gap', 'every licensed relation is inapplicable or slack'). Individual premise-level observations survive.

THEOREM AC stated exactly: for c measurable weak k-colouring, centre x, unit v, finite index type iota, sets K : iota -> Set C, label sets H : iota -> Finset (Fin k), with (H1) every K i is an ApproachingContinuum x (K i) v with the SAME v, (H2) Disjoint (spatialSupport c j) (Straddle (K i)) for j in H i, (H3) (univ \ union H i).card <= 2, the conclusion is False.

AC's eight source citations all resolve: ApproachingContinuum (AngularBoundary:235, common v with r->0+, w->v, point_mem), Straddle (:147), spatialSupport (:308), outer/inner_strip (:244,:252 giving direction-neighbourhood AND radial window), continuum_outer/inner_restriction (:259,:279, used at Exclusion:128-129 and Interfaces:75-76 with E s true / E s false), binary_alternation (BinaryPalettes:11), binary_pair_distinct (:28), binary_strip_palette_rigidity (BoundaryTrace:280, with TWO INDEPENDENT side Bools bu bv and strips at t and t*exp(i pi/3)), outer/inner_strip_trace (:182,:210), angleEssential (:334), angleBoundary (:349), angleBoundary_nonempty (:381, via isPreconnected_univ), angleBoundary_six (:435), sixAngle_injective (:423).
verified_results.grade: source-read with line numbers; the only line-number drift is two lines on sixAngle_injective

verified_results.statement: AC's steps (a)-(d) audited: (a) finite minimum of the strip widths is legitimate via finite_positive_lower_bound as used in continuum_outer_restriction, exceptional set the two perpendiculars; (b) outer for positive and inner for negative scalar product, glued by ae_of_locally_ae, giving BinaryCenter then the flip by binary_alternation; (c) binary_strip_palette_rigidity gives one fixed label in {a,b} on an open angular neighbourhood with independently chosen sides; (d) D subset B u (B - tau) has at most 4 points while angleBoundary_nonempty makes it nonempty and angleBoundary_six puts a six-orbit of distinct points inside it.

Flagged place where care is needed: continuum_*_restriction takes a SINGLE label set J while (H2) gives a different H i per index. Collapsing requires J := intersection over i of (univ \ H i), which under (H3) is {a,b}, and then the hypothesis becomes 'a.e. z in all Straddle (K i) has c z in {a,b}'. That discharges from (H2), but it is the one step a Lean implementation must handle explicitly.
verified_results.grade: PROOF (mine), flagged as the implementation risk

verified_results.statement: What the four-state field lacks, precisely: an actual colouring c : C -> Fin k with WeakColoring; for each i a set K i with a full ApproachingContinuum witness (not just a direction); the a.e. exclusions Disjoint (spatialSupport c j) (Straddle (K i)); and finiteness of the index family. The field supplies none of the four, so it cannot even state AC's hypotheses.

The field's failure is visible exactly where AC bites: step (c) forces one fixed label of {a,b} on an open angular neighbourhood, and the field violates this at t=0, where the label of {0,5} present jumps from 5 (palette {2,5}) to 0 (palette {0,2}). So the field is not a source-level trace field, and its counterexample status is confined to the weaker orbitwise/recurrence reduction.

Consumer checked: q=(0,3,3,3,0,0) gives v_1=v_2=v_3=e^{i pi}=-1, so edges E1={1,2}, E2={2,3}, E3={3,4} share one approach direction as (H1) requires; their endpoints union to {1,2,3,4}, leaving {0,5} of cardinality 2, so AC applies with a=0, b=5 and excludes that configuration for ACTUAL common interfaces.
verified_results.grade: PROOF by inspection of the q-vector

verified_results.statement: Scope: AC is not F6. General direction configurations, including non-aligned vectors, remain open. AC is a paper-level candidate pending independent and Lean review, and its novelty relative to unpublished worker work or the literature has not been investigated.
verified_results.grade: scope statement, matching Astra's own caveat

verified_results.statement: Bank recorded as given: generic contact-ban theorem plus five_support_no_sixty_joint_pair passed Lean 4.34.1/mathlib d13f23b with standard axioms, source SHA 9a904d4d7165889a5b12c77ea4e1646e436a0f5de4d4d057e2ee20d5e6f82ba1; originals unchanged, Lemma 6.7 retained. Not in my read scope; not verified here. The larger three-centre replacement remains a paper candidate.

conjectures: The H i-to-J collapse is the only place AC's Lean implementation could fail, and it is worth pre-checking by hand before any formalisation: the point is that (H3) gives a GLOBAL surviving pair {a,b}, so the per-index label sets can be replaced by their common complement without loss.

AC's hypothesis (H1) forces all approach directions to coincide, which is exactly the alignment the m6 q-vector provides for E1,E2,E3. So the natural next step is to characterise which q-vectors give three consecutive interfaces with a common direction, since only those are touched by AC; all others need an argument that does not assume alignment.

escalation: Exact obstacle: AC closes only the ALIGNED case, where three consecutive interfaces share one approach direction v, because ApproachingContinuum fixes a single v and continuum_*_restriction's side condition is a condition on the single direction v. The m6 q-vector (0,3,3,3,0,0) is aligned, so AC excludes it for actual common interfaces; a q-vector whose three consecutive edges have distinct approach directions is untouched. Definitions used: ApproachingContinuum (AngularBoundary:235), Straddle (:147), spatialSupport (:308), BinaryCenter (BinaryPalettes:9). Expected useful output: either an alignment-free replacement for AC, or a proof that the unaligned case cannot occur for a genuine six-cycle of common interfaces.
